items.title: Emile Barnes, George Guesnon, Little Brother Montgomery, Harold Dejan Interview, 1961-03-11
items.q: I'm going to give you an introduction, a double, and come right in behind the double introduction.

ctx.x: So long, Curly. But see, people don't know nothing about that, Curly, but nobody but me and among us, we music. Curly's George Gano. See you later. Well, George, now I'm going to make you a number for you to remember while I'm going back to Chicago and other places. I've did so much playing around here until I'm fixing to go out of space. I'm going to make you a number for remembers the Satellite Blues.

Well, brother Montgomery, I'll be glad to get those blues and keep them in my repertoire, so be still now. I'm going to give you an introduction, a double, and come right in behind the double introduction.

I've started an invention. Now it might sound silly to you. Now I've started an invention. Now it might sound silly to you. I was only trying to do something that no other man can do. I made a two-monkey carer up with an electronical engine room.

items.title: Eurreal Wilford "Little Brother" Montgomery Interview, 1958-05-29
items.q: We, you know, we had a traveling band. We had quite a jackson. He played all around with me.

ctx.x: Yeah. Also, George Lewis, he and I are good friends.
George Gano. George Gano, that's my buddy.
Yeah, he used to wake me up there. Where did he work with you?
